title: Unified retry-timeline and ergonomic stream adaptor for Py/TS/Go SDKs
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Small breaking-surface avoided; SDKs receive ergonomic retry-timeline config and a lightweight stream adaptor for parity. Patch releases: py 3.8.9 -> 3.8.10, ts 1.6.1 -> 1.6.2, go v1.5.0 -> v1.5.1.
description:
Background: Different SDKs implemented retry/backoff semantics and stream restart heuristics inconsistently, which caused customer-facing flakiness for long-lived streaming sessions and opaque retry behavior under auth window expiry. This PR introduces a cross-language "retry-timeline" contract plus a small, ergonomic stream adaptor that standardizes reconnect/backoff and unblocks the last mile of parity for Py/TS/Go.

What changed (summary): 1) Introduced a common retry-timeline configuration (max_total_duration, initial_backoff_ms, max_backoff_ms, backoff_multiplier, jitter_window_ms) surfaced in each SDK with sane defaults and explicit override. 2) Added a lightweight stream adaptor (StreamResumeAdapter) that centralizes heartbeat handling, credential-refresh hooks, and resume-vs-restart policy decisions. 3) Plumbed telemetry hooks: retry_reason, attempt_index, total_backoff_ms to existing SDK telemetry so platform teams can tie regressions to config changes. 4) Minor API ergonomic additions: Python async iterator helper (.aiter_with_retries()), TypeScript AsyncGenerator wrapper (.withRetryTimeline()), Go StreamHandle.Resume(ctx) convenience. 5) Version bumps for each SDK and unit/integration test matrices updated.

Commits (high level): - decouple: add retry-timeline interface and default implementation across sdk packages - feat(py): aiter_with_retries helper + tests - feat(ts): withRetryTimeline wrapper + examples - feat(go): StreamResumeAdapter + Resume helper - chore: telemetry tags and metrics mapping - test: long-run streaming integration tests (loopback harness) - ci: matrix updates and cross-sdk lint fixes

Files touched (high level): - sdk/common/retry_timeline.proto (contract + docs) - sdk/python/redwood/retry_timeline.py - sdk/python/redwood/stream_adaptor.py - sdk/typescript/src/stream/withRetryTimeline.ts - sdk/go/stream/resume_adapter.go - sdk/*/tests/integration/long_stream_reconnect_test.* - docs/sdk/retry-timeline.md - examples/multi-sdk/stream-reconnect/*

Small illustrative snippet (TypeScript wrapper):
const wrapped = client.stream.open(...).withRetryTimeline({ max_total_duration: 120000, initial_backoff_ms: 100, backoff_multiplier: 2.0 });

Testing and CI: Ran unit tests across all three SDKs and an end-to-end looping harness that simulates auth expiry mid-stream. CI initially failed on TS linter (import ordering) and Go vet on a nil-check; both fixes were added in follow-up commits and CI passed on the final squash. Matrix includes node 16/18, python 3.9/3.10, go 1.20/1.21.

Review highlights / conversation: - Diego Ramirez (reviewer): "Strong +1 for centralizing the timeline — please ensure default values are conservative for high-latency regions." Author: "Defaults chosen after running the loopback against us-west and eu-west latency profiles; documented in retry-timeline.md." - Sofia Chen: "TS ergonomics look good, but add an example with function-calling/resumable tool streams." Author: "Added examples/multi-sdk/stream-reconnect/ts-function-calling.md and accompanying test harness." - Arjun Mehta: "Go Resume helper is convenient but may hide context cancellation semantics; add doc note." Author: "Added doc note and small API comment recommending explicit ctx wiring for callers who expect immediate cancellation." - Diego: "Telemetry tags should be present on all retry exits (success/failed); otherwise we won't be able to attribute regressions." Author: "Added retry_reason and total_backoff_ms tags to post-mortem telemetry path." Review status: approvals from Diego & Sofia; Arjun requested one doc tweak which was addressed.

Backward compatibility and rollout plan: No breaking changes to public surface—new helpers are additive and defaults preserve prior behavior (max_total_duration default is very large). For conservative rollout we gated the TypeScript wrapper behind a feature flag in the hosted SDK registry for two weeks while collecting telemetry. We rolled SDK versions: python 3.8.10, typescript 1.6.2, go v1.5.1. Customers on Dedicated can opt-in to the stricter timeline via console toggle; Private installs receive documentation to manually enable the adaptor.

Why this is unique: Rather than adding language-specific heuristics we define an explicit timeline contract that SDKs implement uniformly; the stream adaptor is intentionally small (thin policy layer) to minimize surface area and improve debuggability.

Follow-ups and TODOs: - ENG-4275: Add example configurations tuned for mobile vs server workloads (tracked). - ENG-4382: Produce benchmark doc showing cost/latency tradeoffs of different timeline settings. - Roll forward the feature flag after 2-week telemetry validation and publish migration notes.

Merge: Squash merged to main after approvals and successful CI.

CI summary: All checks passed on green build (unit + integration + cross-sdk lint).

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps credential plumbing abstract (delegate to SDK credential providers) to remain compatible with existing delegated auth flows. If downstream teams need a deeper integration (e.g., credential prefetch for long streams) we'll follow up with an opt-in extension rather than changing defaults.
